text:
hana: hey all, first week! small Q: our CI runs nightly integration tests that call the API for a few hundred synthetic prompts. Is it okay to use my web-issued sandbox key in CI or should we create a service account / hosted key?

devon: welcome Hana :wave: don't use web-issued user sandbox keys in CI. They expire and are tied to a user. Best is a service account key from Console > API Keys > Service Accounts. Those are auditable and rotatable without touching a person.

mike: +1. For CI use a long-lived service account key and store in the secrets manager (Vault/Secrets Manager). If this is a short experiment and low volume, a sandbox service account is ok; for sustained nightly runs request a hosted dev seat.

hana: ok makes sense. How do quotas work for service accounts vs sandbox user keys?

devon: service accounts map to the quota pool you choose when creating the key — you can pick sandbox or hosted dev. Sandbox pool is shared and stricter (requests/min and tokens/min). Hosted keys are tied to billing and usually have higher per-minute limits. We expose headers to help detect this: X-Quota-Bucket, X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining and Retry-After on 429s.

mike: if your CI bursts hundreds of parallel jobs, you'll hit concurrent request caps even on hosted. Two patterns: 1) run a single controlled worker that de-duplicates and batches tasks, or 2) request a temporary quota bump for the service account and schedule jobs to spread across the minute.

hana: we use GitHub Actions self-hosted runners. Any env var names or SDK config we should standardize on?

devon: use REDWOOD_API_KEY in the runner env and REDWOOD_API_URL if you need to point to sandbox endpoint. In GH Actions store the key as a secret and reference it. Our SDK clients support a retry policy config — set maxRetries=5 and exponential backoff with jitter; always honor Retry-After if present.

infra-bot: FYI: automated note: excessive failed requests from CI may auto-throttle the quota bucket for short cooldowns. See onboarding docs: https://console.redwood.dev/docs/onboarding/ci-best-practices

mike: also log headers in a lightweight way (X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-Quota-Bucket) so you can alert if remaining < 10% and automatically reduce concurrency. That saved us last quarter when a flaky test started spamming the sandbox.

hana: great tips. If we need a temporary bump for the integration window how do we request it?

devon: open a ticket in #help with subject "Temporary quota bump - CI integration" and include account id, service account id, expected tokens/min, window start/end, and contact. Small temporary bumps are usually approved same day. For recurring sustained load we discuss hosted commit.

hana: perfect, i'll create a service account, move the runner secret there, add retries, and open a ticket if we need more. thanks everyone! :raised_hands:
